headline_marked: DeepSeek cuts prices 75% but [[the 100x problem remains]]
headline: DeepSeek cuts prices 75% but the 100x problem remains
summary: AI model price drops don't ease enterprise costs due to token amplification
details: DeepSeek's 75% price cut on its V4-Pro model hasn't eased enterprise AI costs. The issue lies in token amplification, where agent systems consume tokens faster than prices drop.

The '100x problem' refers to the vast difference in cost between serving a user request as a chatbot versus an agentic workflow. A single user-visible request can cost much more to serve as an agentic workflow.
In a single-turn chatbot, one user message produces roughly one model call. In a multi-step agent, that ratio can land at 1:700 or higher, leading to significantly higher costs.
The dominant pricing story for enterprise AI has been seat-based SaaS, but token amplification breaks this assumption. Vendor gross margins can turn negative as customers deepen their agent adoption.
caption:
Can AI models get cheap enough? DeepSeek's 75% price cut doesn't solve the 100x problem

DeepSeek's 75% price cut on its V4-Pro model hasn't eased enterprise AI costs. The issue lies in token amplification, where agent systems consume tokens faster than prices drop.

The '100x problem' refers to the vast difference in cost between serving a user request as a chatbot versus an agentic workflow. A single user-visible request can cost much more to serve as an agentic workflow.

In a single-turn chatbot, one user message produces roughly one model call. In a multi-step agent, that ratio can land at 1:700 or higher, leading to significantly higher costs.

The dominant pricing story for enterprise AI has been seat-based SaaS, but token amplification breaks this assumption. Vendor gross margins can turn negative as customers deepen their agent adoption.
